title: fix(metadata-protocol): fold publishMetaItem through canonicalizeMetaRequestType (#8769)
body:
Fixes #8769

`canonicalizeMetaRequestType` is the `/meta` request boundary, and its own header calls it the fold "all six entry points funnel through". `publishMetaItem` is a **seventh** entry point on the same URL family and did not funnel through it — it reached the draftability check through `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR`, the MANIFEST-collection map, which is the exact lookup #7894 replaced at the other six. One contract, two dialects, decided by which verb you used (Prime Directive #12).

The fix is the same one line the other six carry, at the top of the method.

## Resumed work — every claim re-derived

The implementation commit was written by an agent killed by a container restart before it ran anything, so its comment stated intent as measurement, and `main` had moved three times underneath it (#8747, #8671, #8786 all landed in this file). `main` is merged, every line number re-derived on the merged tree, and two claims the draft carried did not survive and were corrected rather than inherited. Details in the second commit's message.

## What the fold actually reaches — measured, and NOT uniform

The card filed this as pure coherence, "fail-closed today, nothing minted, nothing bypassed", on the reading that a plural-addressed publish looks for a row under the plural `type` and finds none. **That reading is right for the four manifest-absent types and wrong for the manifest-present ones**, because `promoteDraftForPublish` folds through the manifest map *before* the row lookup.

**The four manifest-absent types — fail-closed, but closed for the wrong reason and with the wrong verdict.** `field`, `seed`, `external_catalog` and `translation` are legitimately absent from `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` (they are not stack collections; that absence is exactly why #7894 moved the boundary onto the URL map). Unfolded, they arrived at the draftability check as unrecognised, where `isRuntimeCreateAllowed`'s "no static registry entry, so this is a plugin-registered kind" arm answers **true** — the permissive plugin branch, taken for a type the platform itself declares. A publish addressed `/meta/fields/showcase_task.title` PASSED a gate that `/meta/field/...` answers `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE`, and only died further down on `404 no_draft`, having already forgotten which type it was judging.

**Manifest-present types — one lookup that did NOT fail closed.** `getEffectiveLock`'s artifact limb folds; its **overlay limb queries `sys_metadata` with the raw `type`**. Addressed with a plural, the ADR-0010 `_lock` carried by the stored active row was looked up under a `type` no row has and came back `'none'` — not a neutral value, but the verdict "the author declared no protection" (#5706) — while the promote one line later read the folded key and overwrote the row the lock protected.

Stated at its real width rather than rounded up: that window needs an environment kernel (the gate is skipped wholesale when `environmentId` is `undefined`), a lock carried by a *stored overlay* row rather than a packaged artifact, and a draft predating the lock (the save door refuses to mint one once the lock is live). Within it, a lock gate could be addressed around from the wire.

## ZONE 2 — the PM's redundancy expectation, falsified

The dispatch expected `promoteDraftForPublish`'s manifest fold to become **redundant**. Measured, it does not, and it is **kept**:

- On the `publishMetaItem` path it is an exact no-op — verified, not assumed: no canonical singular is also a key of `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` (measured: the intersection is empty), so `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR[canonical] ?? canonical` is the identity.
- It is load-bearing for the helper's **other** caller, `publishPackageDrafts`, which feeds it `d.type` from stored draft rows. That is data at rest, where a legacy row written under a plural `type` is real and nothing rewrites it on upgrade — a different input class needing a different map, exactly as `canonicalMetaType`'s header describes. Deleting it as "now redundant" would have changed the batch path.

Applying the *request* fold there would be worse than a no-op: `canonicalizeMetaRequestType` **throws** `400 INVALID_REQUEST` on an unrecognised spelling, so pointing it at stored rows would convert legacy data into a hard refusal.

## The `publishPackageDrafts` / `deletePackage` question — answered, both negative

Neither needs a fold: **neither takes a caller-supplied `type` at all** (both are addressed by `packageId`). The per-row work is already covered — `deletePackage` routes every row through `deleteMetaItem`, which folds; `publishPackageDrafts` reaches the manifest-map fold above. The card's hypothesis was right, for a firmer reason than the one it gave.

## Verification

Pinned in `packages/objectql/src/protocol-publish-canonical-fold.test.ts` against a real `ObjectQL`, the real protocol and the real `SysMetadataRepository` over an in-memory driver, reading back the stored **row** rather than only the receipt. Three groups: a manifest-absent plural (`translations`) resolving the canonical row, the draftability gate judging the real registry entry (`fields`), and the overlay `_lock` (`views`) — each with a discriminating control in the same group, plus a `translationz` control proving the boundary folds a *declared* spelling rather than having become tolerant of anything ending in `s`.

**Why the pin is not co-located with the code.** `metadata-protocol` cannot import `ObjectQL` — `objectql` depends on `metadata-protocol`, not the reverse — and this seam is only observable against a real engine. It is the same package and the same reason as the existing fold pins for the other six entry points in `protocol-meta-type-canonicalization.test.ts`, and the same split the co-located `protocol.audit-org-scope.test.ts` states in its own header.

**Reverse verification** — direction predicted before running, against a REBUILT `dist` (the suite resolves the package through `dist`, so a source-only revert measures nothing while looking like it did). Predicted 3 red / 4 green; measured 3 red / 4 green, each red for its predicted reason:

```
x A `translations` promotes the draft written under `translation`
  -> [no_draft] No pending draft exists for translations/zh_cn
x B `fields` is refused by the draftability gate
  -> expected 'NO_DRAFT' to be 'NOT_OVERRIDABLE'   (the gate had PASSED)
x C the plural spelling is refused by the SAME lock
  -> expected a refusal, got success                (the locked publish went through)
Tests  3 failed | 4 passed (7)
```

Restored and rebuilt, 7/7 green. Note for anyone repeating it: verify the ablation reached `dist` with an **executable** marker, never a comment — tsup strips comments, so a prose marker is absent in both directions and proves nothing. Here the marker is the call count: `grep -o canonicalizeMetaRequestType dist/index.js | wc -l` is 8 with the fix (one definition, seven call sites) and 7 without.

## Gates and ledgers — all at `01f270e6d`

Union re-run after the final commit. `check:changeset-gate-self-tests`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:durability-log-level`, `check:filter-alias-parity`, `check:objectui-changeset`, `check:query-options-erasure`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-empty-changeset`, `check-engine-split-ratio` — all PASS. Tests: `metadata-protocol` 1389/1389, `objectql` 3663/3663.

Both ratchets measured **directly**, because a green `pnpm typecheck` proves nothing here — `packages/objectql/tsconfig.json` excludes `**/*.test.ts`, so tsc never sees the new file:

- `@objectstack/objectql` TEST_DEBT — recorded 355, measured **355**, with **0** errors attributable to the new test file.
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` DEBT — recorded 63, measured **63**, with **0** in `protocol.ts`.

## Out of scope, filed not fixed

- **#8819** — `rollbackMetaItem` is an **eighth** `/meta` entry point with the identical shape: manifest fold for the row operations, raw `type` into the same ADR-0010 gate. Reachable as `POST /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/rollback`. Filed unlabeled for triage; it also raises whether the durable fix belongs at `getEffectiveLock` instead, which is a shared gate and a maintainer's call.
- **#8820** — `ensureObjectStorage`'s `'objects'` limb is now dormant (both call sites stand behind a fold). Observation-class, `finding` label.

`canonicalizeMetaRequestType` itself is untouched — that is PR #8770's parked region.
